region: Cutchogue · North Fork of Long Island, New York
about: Lieb Cellars has been part of the North Fork since 1992, when Mark and Kathy Lieb started it on the farmland around Cutchogue, at the eastern end of Long Island. Russell Hearn, the Australian-born winemaker who shaped the label from 1993 on, bought it with partners in 2023 and joined it with his family’s Suhru wines. The estate, recently renamed Rooted North, is run by the Hearn family, including Susan Hearn, Shelby Hearn Ulrich and assistant winemaker Brad Ulrich.

Merlot is the North Fork’s signature red. The region’s maritime climate, with water on three sides, gives a long, moderate growing season that suits it. Lieb’s Estate Merlot comes from the family’s sustainably farmed vineyards and spends ten months in Hungarian oak barrels before bottling. Hungarian oak is tighter-grained and gentler than new American oak, so it supports the fruit rather than masking it. The winery bottles it as an approachable, medium-bodied red that it says will also age well.

Astor Wines describes the 2022 as medium-bodied, with plush dark fruit and ripe berry aromas. Expect dark cherry and cranberry on the nose, then ripe plum and a touch of graphite over fine, elegant tannins. The winery describes its Estate Merlot as soft and fruity with a smooth finish, and suggests pairing it with charcuterie, pork, red meat and roasted vegetables.
